title: Exploring DAOS Interfaces and Performance
problem: Applications need diverse I/O access patterns from native object APIs to POSIX file systems, and the performance characteristics of different interface layers on NVM-backed distributed storage remain unclear.
motivation: Understanding interface trade-offs is critical for deploying high-performance distributed storage systems on modern NVM hardware.
method: DAOS provides both a native object storage API and FUSE-based POSIX file system interface over NVM devices. The paper benchmarks both interfaces with various I/O workloads and compares performance against a distributed file system and competing object storage system on the same hardware.
key_novelty: Systematic quantification of performance trade-offs between high-performance native object APIs and standard POSIX interfaces through FUSE on NVM-backed distributed storage.
contributions: Characterization of DAOS native API versus FUSE interface performance across different I/O access patterns
Comparative evaluation against distributed file systems and competing object storage platforms
Quantification of interface abstraction costs on NVM-based storage performance
Demonstration of DAOS flexibility in supporting multiple I/O interfaces with performance visibility

metrics.speedup: I/O throughput and latency improvements versus distributed file system and object store baselines
metrics.other: Bandwidth utilization and per-operation latency metrics across different access patterns
